notes.title: 말을 놓다
notes.text: Switching to casual speech (반말) is a real milestone in a Korean friendship. Usually the older person offers: 말 놓을까? or 편하게 말해. Never switch on your own with someone older — and keep using polite speech with elders like Grandma.

notes.title: Writing letters
notes.text: Korean letters start with "[name]에게" (to…), or "[name]께" for elders, and often end with "[name]가/이가" (from…). Byeol's letters begin with 오빠에게 — "To my older brother."

lessons.goal: Switch between casual speech and humble honorifics.

notes.title: Humble verbs
notes.text: When the person you're talking TO is older, you lower yourself: 말씀드리다 (tell, humbly), 여쭈다 (ask), 뵙다 (see/meet), 드리다 (give). Grandma, in turn, speaks 반말 to the young boarders — that's normal and affectionate.
